stem: What does the displayed mglearn.plot_single_hidden_layer_graph() call establish, separate from importing MLPRegressor?
assumptions: The snippet presumes mglearn and display are available; their setup is not shown, and no execution of that unavailable plotting dependency is claimed.

options.text: It creates an unfitted MLPRegressor configured with the later 256, 256, 128 hidden widths
It visualizes the fitted connection weights of the later robot-arm regressor
It displays a generic architecture graph, without configuring or fitting the later robot-arm regressor

citations.evidenceText:
What is MLP Regression?


In scikit-learn, MLP Regression is the estimator class used to
implement Multilayer Perceptron (MLPs) for regression tasks.
•  MLPs, Multilayer perceptron are also known as (vanilla) feed-
   forward neural networks, or sometimes just neural
   networks.
•  The architecture of an MLP for regression consists of an input
    layer, one or more hidden layers, and an output layer.
•   Multilayer perceptron is for classification and regression,
   serve as a starting point for more involved deep learning
   methods.

solution.justification: An illustrative graph is neither the later configured estimator nor its fitted weights. No training arrays or fitted regressor are supplied to this call.

optionExplanations.o1: Incorrect. A generic diagram call is not construction of that estimator; the later model constructor supplies those widths.
optionExplanations.o2: Incorrect. No fitted robot-arm model is passed to this illustrative graph function, so the drawing is not evidence of fitted weights.
optionExplanations.o3: Correct. The graph illustrates network structure; estimator construction and model.fit are separate operations.
